text:
Brett Howden scored 25 seconds into the game on a 3% chance, and VGK never gave the lead back. That goal set the tone for a 6-2 win in which Vegas was only slightly better on paper (54% to deserve the win, 3.94 expected goals to CGY's 3.7) but far better where it counted. The gap came from finishing and goaltending. Dustin Wolf allowed 2.1 more goals than the 33 shots he faced should have cost him, while Carter Hart stopped 28 of 30 and saved 1.7 goals above expected.

Calgary had the better of the even-strength play, 2.96 expected goals to 1.79, and out-attempted Vegas 63 to 60. The Flames also won the first and third periods on chance quality. But Jack Eichel's shorthanded wrist shot in the first made it 2-0, and when Jake Middleton answered shorthanded in the second, Braeden Bowman restored the two-goal margin on a power play 48 seconds later. Vegas out-chanced Calgary 2.69 to 0.96 in that period, and Bowman also missed a 28% look.

Mark Stone settled it in the third. He tipped in a Eichel pass 66 seconds into the period, added a backhand at 12:10, and completed the hat trick on a power play with 3:47 left, assisted by Eichel and Mitch Marner. Ivan Barbashev set up three goals, and Eichel finished with a goal and two assists. Matt Coronato's power-play goal at 18:40 only trimmed the final margin.
